primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum due to ABCC6 deficiency
mechanism: ABCC6 deficiency is associated with low circulating inorganic pyrophosphate, reducing an important inhibitor of mineralization and permitting ectopic calcification of elastic tissues in skin, retina, and blood vessels.
vignette: A 19-year-old woman has clusters of yellow papules on the lateral neck and flexural skin. Ophthalmologic examination shows angioid streaks. A skin biopsy demonstrates fragmented, calcified elastic fibers. Molecular testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in ABCC6.
lead: Which of the following biochemical abnormalities most directly promotes the tissue changes in this disorder?
correct: Reduced circulating inorganic pyrophosphate, permitting ectopic mineralization
distractors: Deficient copper delivery to lysyl oxidase, impairing collagen cross-linking
Reduced synthesis of fibrillin-1, causing abnormal microfibril formation
Defective type VII collagen anchoring fibrils at the dermal-epidermal junction
Excess degradation of elastin by neutrophil elastase in the lung and skin
distractor_notes: Impaired copper-dependent lysyl oxidase is characteristic of Menkes disease and causes defective connective-tissue cross-linking, not ABCC6-related ectopic mineralization.
Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome and abnormal microfibrils rather than the low-pyrophosphate mineralization mechanism of pseudoxanthoma elasticum.
Type VII collagen defects cause dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa with defective anchoring fibrils and skin fragility, not calcification of elastic fibers.
Unchecked neutrophil elastase is central to alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency–related emphysema; it does not explain ABCC6-associated systemic elastic-tissue mineralization.
key_expl: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum is caused by biallelic ABCC6 pathogenic variants. Disease-associated low circulating inorganic pyrophosphate removes a physiologic brake on mineralization, permitting calcification of elastic tissues in the skin, eye, and vascular system.
objective: Connect ABCC6 deficiency in pseudoxanthoma elasticum with reduced inorganic pyrophosphate and ectopic elastic-tissue mineralization.
